original: Atuona is the main village on Hiva Oa, the second-largest island in the Marquesas archipelago
final_text: Atuona is the main village of Hiva Oa, the second-largest Marquesas island (about 320 sq km), and the administrative centre of the southern Marquesas.
source_note: Second largest Marquesas island, 320 km2; Atuona admin centre

original: Located in French Polynesia, 1,400 km northeast of Tahiti
final_text: Atuona lies in French Polynesia, about 1,400 km northeast of Tahiti; Britannica puts the Marquesas group as a whole about 1,200 km away.
source_note: Britannica: Marquesas 1,200 km NE of Tahiti

original: Coordinates: 9°48'S, 139°02'W - literally the edge of the world
final_text: Atuona sits at about 9°48'S, 139°02'W, on the south coast of Hiva Oa.
source_note: Coordinates 9°48′11″S 139°2′23″W

original: Population: ~2,000 people, mostly Polynesian Marquesans
final_text: Atuona had 1,993 inhabitants at the 2022 census, most of them Marquesan.
source_note: Population 1,993 (2022)

original: The name "Hiva Oa" means "long ridgeback" in Marquesan
final_text: In local Marquesan tradition, the name Hiva Oa means long ridge.
source_note: Local mythology: Hiva Oa means long ridge

original: Dramatic volcanic peaks rising from the Pacific - Mount Temetiu (1,276m) dominates
final_text: Mount Temetiu, the island summit at about 1,213 m (sources range up to 1,276 m), towers over Atuona and the western end of the Bay of Traitors.
source_note: Wikipedia gives 1,213 m; Hiva Oa page 1,269 m

original: Lush valleys with breadfruit, mango, coconut palms, hibiscus
final_text: Hiva Oa is called the Garden of the Marquesas; its people live largely on breadfruit, coconut, yam and taro they grow themselves.
source_note: Nickname Garden of the Marquesas; subsistence crops per Wikipedia

original: Black sand beaches, hidden coves, ancient stone tikis in the jungle
final_text: At the me'ae of Iipona in Puamau, across Hiva Oa from Atuona, stands Takaii, a stone tiki over 2.4 m tall, the largest in Polynesia.
source_note: Takai over 2.4 m, largest tiki in Polynesia

original: Constant trade winds, tropical humidity, sudden rain showers
final_text: Atuona sits on a small inlet, Vevau in Marquesan, on the north shore of Ta'a Oa, the wide bay the French call Baie des Traitres; the rocky islet Hanakee guards it.
source_note: Bay names, Vevau inlet, Hanakee islet

original: The light here is different - golden, soft, the light Gauguin sought
final_text: The bay at Atuona, Ta'aoa or the Bay of Traitors, lies inside the crater of the old volcano that built this side of Hiva Oa.
source_note: Ta'aoa bay is in the crater of the volcano

original: Smell of frangipani, salt air, wood smoke from copra drying
final_text: Copra, dried coconut meat, is the cash export of Hiva Oa, produced alongside a subsistence economy of breadfruit, coconut, yam and taro.
source_note: Economy: subsistence crops plus copra for export

original: Marquesan culture: tattoo tradition (oldest in Polynesia), wood carving, tapa cloth
final_text: Marquesan tattoo, patutiki, could cover whole bodies; in 1897-98 German physician Karl von den Steinen recorded hundreds of its motifs as colonisation was ending the practice.
source_note: Whole-body tattoo; von den Steinen 1897-98; oldest claim dropped

original: The "Pua" - traditional feast with roasted pig, poi, breadfruit
final_text: Marquesan feasts were ko'ika; their staple was ma, breadfruit paste fermented in deep pits for long storage and eaten as popoi.
source_note: Feasts called ko'ika, not pua; ma fermented breadfruit

original: Catholic church (where Gauguin is buried) mixed with ancient beliefs in "mana" (spiritual power)
final_text: Gauguin is buried not in a church but in the hillside Calvary (Calvaire) cemetery above Atuona; he had bought his house plot from the Catholic mission.
source_note: Calvary Cemetery overlooks town; land bought from Church

original: Time moves differently - "Polynesian time" - nothing is rushed
final_text: Atuona was once the seat of government for all the Marquesas, a role later taken by Taiohae on Nuku Hiva.
source_note: Former Marquesas capital, replaced by Taioha'e

original: The locals say: "Kaoha nui" (great love) as greeting
final_text: The everyday Marquesan greeting is kaoha, used much as aloha in Hawaii; kaoha nui (nui, great) is the warmer, fuller form.
source_note: Kaoha = hello/welcome; nui adds warmth

original: Art is life here - every house has carvings, every body has tattoos
final_text: The Matavaa, the Awakening, a Marquesas arts festival founded in 1987 by the Motu Haka federation, rotates among the six inhabited islands, Hiva Oa among them.
source_note: Created 1987 by Motu Haka; rotates six islands

original: His "Maison du Jouir" (House of Pleasure) - now reconstructed museum
final_text: The Maison du Jouir (House of Pleasure) was rebuilt in Atuona as part of the Paul Gauguin Cultural Center, completed in 2003.
source_note: Paul Gauguin Cultural Center completed 2003

original: Original was bamboo and palm fronds, decorated with his explicit carvings
final_text: The original was a two-storey thatched house on stilts; its carved door panels, inscribed Maison du Jouir, Soyez mysterieuses and Soyez amoureuses, are now in the Musee d'Orsay.
source_note: Orsay: cabin on stilts, carved inscribed panels

original: He lived there 1901-1903, painting his final masterpieces
final_text: He lived at Atuona from September 1901 until May 1903; Riders on the Beach and Contes barbares, both 1902 and now in the Museum Folkwang, Essen, were painted there.
source_note: Arrived Sept 1901; Folkwang holds both 1902 works

original: Died May 8, 1903 at 54 - syphilis, morphine addiction, broken heart
final_text: He died at Atuona on 8 May 1903, aged 54, cause still debated; teeth dug from his well in 2000 held no mercury, the usual syphilis cure of his day.
source_note: Broken heart unverifiable; teeth DNA 90-99%, no mercury

original: His grave overlooks the bay he painted so many times
final_text: His grave of unhewn pinkish stones in Calvary cemetery looks over Atuona Bay; a bronze cast of his Oviri was set on it on 29 March 1973; Jacques Brel lies a few metres away.
source_note: Oviri bronze erected 29 March 1973; Brel nearby

original: From Paris: 30+ hours - Paris → Los Angeles → Tahiti → Hiva Oa
final_text: From Paris, Air Tahiti Nui flies to Papeete via Los Angeles, its only Paris stopover since Seattle was dropped in January 2025; Air Tahiti then flies on to Hiva Oa.
source_note: Paris route refocused via LA; 30+ hours unsourced

original: From Tahiti: 3.5-hour flight on small ATR-72 plane
final_text: From Papeete, Air Tahiti ATR 72s fly to Hiva Oa in well over 3 hours, among the longest legs on its network.
source_note: Papeete-Hiva Oa exceeds 3 hours scheduled

original: Or by cargo ship "Aranui 5" - 14-day voyage through all Marquesas
final_text: By sea: the Aranui 5, a passenger-freighter in service since December 2015, makes a 14-day loop from Papeete through the six inhabited Marquesas, Hiva Oa included.
source_note: Cargo cruise since Dec 2015; 14-day itinerary

original: The airport is tiny, carved into a mountain
final_text: Hiva Oa-Atuona airport, also called Jacques Brel airport, sits on the Tepuna plateau above town, with a single asphalt runway 1,215 m long.
source_note: Runway 1,215 m; Brel name and plateau per Kupi

original: Landing feels like arriving at the end of the earth
final_text: Jacques Brel, who sailed in in 1975, used his light plane Jojo to fly the sick to Nuku Hiva and fetch mail and medicine; Jojo now sits in the Espace Jacques Brel hangar.
source_note: Brel 1975, Jojo flights, displayed in hangar
